title: Watch 150 Classic Horror and Suspense Films Free Online: Nosferatu, The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, Carnival of Souls, Night of the Living Dead & More

body:
﻿
From rough­ly the mid-nine­teen-fifties through the mid-nine­teen-sev­en­ties, the avail­abil­i­ty of air­time on Amer­i­can tele­vi­sion sta­tions exceed­ed their capac­i­ty to fill it with high-qual­i­ty orig­i­nal pro­gram­ming. This was espe­cial­ly true in the hours when rel­a­tive­ly few view­ers were awake to tune in, a con­di­tion that gave rise to the late-night movie show. Spe­cial­iz­ing in less­er Hol­ly­wood pro­duc­tions and the releas­es of by-then for­got­ten stu­dios, these pro­grams came to con­sti­tute home revival hous­es, and often eccen­tric ones. By its very nature, the reper­toire of yes­ter­year’s “B movies” con­sist­ed most­ly of genre pic­tures, and no genre proved as pop­u­lar among this par­tic­u­lar view­er­ship as hor­ror. Hence the even­tu­al pop­u­lar­i­ty of hosts like Vam­pi­ra, Ghoular­di, and, lat­er, the icon­ic Elvi­ra, Mis­tress of the Dark.
Wide­ly rec­og­nized as hav­ing inspired gen­er­a­tions of film­mak­ers, writ­ers, and artists, the late-night movie show also pro­vid­ed ordi­nary view­ers with glimpses of film his­to­ry and cul­ture they’d nev­er get oth­er­wise. And though its time may be long since over, you can still expe­ri­ence a ver­sion of it this Hal­loween, or on any oth­er night, through sources like the Youtube playlist above.
It col­lects about 150 hor­ror and sus­pense films that, whether fright­en­ing, kitschy, fun­ny, or some com­bi­na­tion of those qual­i­ties, could well have been local­ly broad­cast to the will­ing insom­ni­acs of 50, 60, 70 years ago. Revenge of the Zom­bies, The Mon­ster Mak­er, Fangs of the Liv­ing Dead, The Brain That Would­n’t Die, Were­wolf in a Girl’s Dor­mi­to­ry: with movies like these, the enter­tain­ment — and the entice­ment to stay tuned, no mat­ter the hour — began right there in the title.
Not that this is a playlist of guilty plea­sures alone. Silent pic­tures like The Cab­i­net of Dr. Cali­gari, The Golem, Nos­fer­atu, and Häx­an con­tin­ue to be scru­ti­nized by film-stud­ies schol­ars as foun­da­tion­al to not just mod­ern hor­ror cin­e­ma but the visu­al lan­guage of cin­e­ma itself. How­ev­er strait­ened their bud­gets, nine­teen-six­ties fea­tures like Car­ni­val of Souls, Night of the Liv­ing Dead, The Inno­cents (a favorite of Mar­tin Scors­ese), and the Edgar Allan Poe adap­ta­tion The Masque of the Red Death are now cred­it­ed with mer­its tran­scend­ing their genre. But even the less ret­ro­spec­tive­ly ele­vat­ed likes of The Mur­der in the Muse­um, The Earth Dies Scream­ing, The Lit­tle Shop of Hor­rors, and The Psy­chopath lurid­ly demon­strate that hor­ror could be mixed with mys­tery, sci­ence fic­tion, com­e­dy, and psy­cho­log­i­cal dra­ma. The pow­er of that hybrid­i­ty was what late-night movie shows impressed on their most dis­cern­ing view­ers — which is to say, their least dis­cern­ing ones.

title: 'The Encyclopedia of Movie Cats' Is an Exhaustive Index of Every Feline to Prowl on Screen
description: Mr. Bigglesworth, Jinxy, Keanu, and Thackery Binx all scamper back into the limelight in a new catalog of felines on screen. Released this month f
body:
Mr. Bigglesworth, Jinxy, Keanu, and Thackery Binx all scamper back into the limelight in a new catalog of felines on screen. Released this month from A24, The Encyclopedia of Movie Cats is a playful, exhaustive compendium of the four-legged friends that have appeared in films throughout the ages. From main characters to helpful sidekicks to the accomplices of villains, these furry actors are iconic in their roles, sometimes even stealing the show from their human counterparts.
The Encyclopedia of Movie Cats features more than 700 felines across 1,900 stills. Get your copy in the Colossal Shop.

title: A Rare Disease and Analog Photography Merge in a Portrait of Self-Discovery
description: “Everything Twice” is a quiet meditation on disability and the ways we orient ourselves in the world. Since childhood, Cy Kuckenbaker noticed that
body:
“Everything Twice” is a quiet meditation on disability and the ways we orient ourselves in the world. Since childhood, Cy Kuckenbaker noticed that one of his eyes drooped, something he attributed to a snowboarding accident. But doctors quickly dismissed that theory, and after innumerable tests and many, many years, the photographer learned he was born with a rare disease.
Kuckenbaker chronicles this realization alongside a slow, analog process he began to combat burnout. Utilizing homemade cameras crafted from cardboard boxes and drugstore magnifying glasses, he captured a variety of landscapes and sights on the West Coast. Pairing both the slow processes of labor-intensive photography with that of uncovering an unusual ailment creates a short film that’s equal part self-discovery and contemplation on disconnection and loss.

title: Timothy Boomer Captures the Uncanny World of Insect Galls
description: Gall wasps, also known as cynipids, have a unique mutual relationship with plants. Their name is derived from the deposits, called galls, which th
body:
Gall wasps, also known as cynipids, have a unique mutual relationship with plants. Their name is derived from the deposits, called galls, which they induce on host plants to support their larvae. The benign growths are created by chemicals that the larvae insert into the plant, drawing on its resources. These phenomena are often very tiny, occasionally appear in clusters, and can range from ruddy brown to vibrant pinks and yellows. Nature photographer Timothy Boomer can’t get enough of them.
“Galls can be brought about by many different organisms, but I tend to focus on the ones induced by cynipid wasps because they are the most visually stunning (at least in my opinion),” Boomer tells Colossal.
Striped volcano gall induced by the cynipid wasp (Feron atrimentum, formerly Andricus atrimentus), Solano County, California
A gall serves as both protection and a food source for the insect growing inside. If all goes according to plan, the larva remains safe from predators, receives enough food, and grows into an adult before climbing out and continuing the cycle. Different species of wasp create unique characteristics, often on very specific parts of the plants. Scientists believe there are at least around 1,300 cynipids globally.
Sometimes, environmental effects change the nodules’ appearance. Boomer points to the spined turban gall, which typically has a bubblegum-pink hue with spines protruding from a relatively flat center. He also captured an atypical one, which is a darker pink with blackened tips and spikes all over. “In this case, normal development was interrupted by a non-inducer entering the gall at an early stage,” Boomer says. “I’m not a scientist, so I won’t pretend to fully comprehend the intricacies of how all this plays out, but I think of it as a ‘home invasion’ that actually alters the home.”
At such minuscule scale with shallow depth-of-field, Boomer uses a focus-stacking technique, which involves taking hundreds, sometimes thousands of images and layering them digitally to make the tiny objects clear. He edits minimally in Photoshop to retain the integrity of the original scene and is passionate about sharing only what occurs naturally. Essentially, he lets the beautiful, bizarre geometries be what they are. “Nature does not need to be ‘enhanced,'” he says.
Find Boomer’s work on Instagram, where you can explore slime molds, flowers, and more.

title: Escape into Gretchen Scherer's Maximalist Paintings of Palatial, Art-Filled Spaces
description: Gretchen Scherer’s paintings of affluent homes, studios, and libraries appear to expand before our eyes. Brimming with ornately framed paintings i
body:
Gretchen Scherer’s paintings of affluent homes, studios, and libraries appear to expand before our eyes. Brimming with ornately framed paintings installed salon-style on richly papered walls, her half-imagined spaces are inspired by real places, which she infuses with a playful brightness and whimsy.
When we home in on one particular floral arrangement, framed artwork, or piece of furniture, it seems that there’s a sudden increase in how much more there is to explore. Scherer’s new solo exhibition, In Time at Monya Rowe Gallery, continues the artist’s fascination with historical interiors, from art museums and drawing rooms to palatial halls and ecclesiastical spaces.
“A French Cafe with Paintings” (2026), oil and acrylic on panel, 18 x 24 inches
Each canvas is devoid of figures other than those depicted in portraits, but there is always the sense that someone has been very busy. The artist leans into a kind of escapism or longing for not only elegant, luminous surroundings but a desire to immerse oneself, quite literally, in the world of art. In our era of steel, glass, concrete, and contractor gray interiors, Scherer celebrates craftsmanship and beauty.
Fantastical convergences of art history and architecture occur in pieces like “A French Cafe with Paintings,” where a Beaux Arts interior transforms into an ad hoc gallery with myriad famous works casually strewn about. Gustav Klimt’s “The Kiss” (1908-09) leans to the right, while Henri Toulouse-Lautrec’s “At the Moulin Rouge” (1892-95) sits nearby.
Working in oil, Scherer’s choice of media nods to the same used to create many of the historical examples she includes. And as we increasingly contend with barrages of digital information and generative AI, the artist inundates us instead with the purely analog and handmade. It begs the question: in another 100 years, what will humans have been producing in our time that merits the same kind of awe and respect we have for these earlier creations?
In Time opens today and continues through January 9 in New York. See more on Scherer’s Instagram.

title: 17th-Century Embroidery Meets Hand-Carved Wooden Vessels by Aspen Golann
description: In the second half of the 17th century, when early American colonists were well into producing their own furniture, makers drew upon the motifs an
body:
In the second half of the 17th century, when early American colonists were well into producing their own furniture, makers drew upon the motifs and techniques common in England. Chests and cabinets were chunky, and chairs and tables often incorporated spool-like legs. In Boston, a particular interpretation of the high-backed Windsor chair emerged, inspiring furniture-maker and artist Aspen Golann to create uniquely sculptural, contemporary iterations as a nod to this heritage.
“Meeting Bench,” made in collaboration with chairmaker Peter Galbert, and “Union Settee” pay tribute to the unique early style while also celebrating furniture’s role in how we convene. Golann has long been interested in the relationships between form and function, in addition to the connections between people and the objects they use, which she also continues to explore through a series of imaginitive brushes and brooms.
“Meeting Bench”
Golann’s interest in early American furniture led to another centuries-old craft tradition: embroidery. Her research into early needlework, an activity pursued almost exclusively by women, inspired an ongoing series of wooden vessels she began making as part of the The Metropolitan Museum of Art and Vacheron Constantin Artisan Residency. The program runs for 18 months and emphasizes the preservation and reinterpretation of traditional craft techniques. Golann was also joined by ceramicist Ibrahim Said and jeweler Joy Harvey.
Utilitarian at their most essential, vessels are also often displayed for strictly decorative purposes, and the artist has been increasingly interested in nudging the boundary between functionality and aesthetic appeal. Pieces like “Pouring Vessel” interpret needlework motifs onto solid wood using a strapworking technique. Even the pancaked “Strap-Carved Vessel” is hollow, so it doesn’t forego its fundamental condition. Its whimsical flatness draws our attention instead to its ornate design, which is the point.
Historically, the sewn compositions made by young girls haven’t gotten a lot of attention, at least not within the context of major art institutions. “[The embroidery] is under-researched and under-displayed, and it’s fragile, rare, and stowable,” Golann says. “I wanted to make some version of this thing that couldn’t be put away.”
Completed during residency, “Crewel Cabinet” stands five feet, four inches tall—about the average height of an American woman. The artist composed the cabinet with 37 staves, or thin strips of wood that connect edge-to-edge to create a rounded form, and each stave is meticulously built from 14 colored layers. From these layers, Golann has carved plants, rabbits, dogs, and more, where the changing colors evoke the vibrant threads within colonial-era crewel embroidery. 
“Crewel Cabinet”
“These embroideries were often dowry objects, made within restrictive expectations for women’s lives,” Golann says. She adds:

Their compositions and themes could be quite consistent, but they are also material evidence of the girls’ internal lives and creative expression. They’re full of sensitivity, affection, and interest in the natural world, but they’re also bizarre, strange, and imaginative. I’ve been trying to tune my sensitivity to the frequency of their imaginations and lived experience, then splash that over a much larger, more expressive canvas.

Golann’s next project will be for the U.S. Treasury, which commissions a piece of furniture for its collection every 50 years. “I’m using different tones of precious metals, applied in a paint-by-numbers way, to create an abstracted, bizarre landscape inspired by early American embroidery,” the artist says. The work will incorporate reflective surfaces so that viewers will see themselves mirrored in the scene. She’s also currently working toward a solo exhibition, slated to open next November, at the Fuller Craft Museum.
“Crewel Cabinet” will be on view as part of the group exhibition Pattern Recognition: Superhouse at Five, opening November 6 and continuing through December 19 at Superhouse in New York City. See more on Golann’s Instagram.

title: November 2026 Opportunities: Open Calls, Residencies, and Grants for Artists
description: Every month, we share opportunities for artists and designers, including open calls, grants, fellowships, and residencies. Make sure you never mis
body:
Every month, we share opportunities for artists and designers, including open calls, grants, fellowships, and residencies. Make sure you never miss out by joining our monthly Opportunities Newsletter.
$4,500 Artist GrantsFeaturedThe Hopper Prize is now accepting entries for $4,500 and $1,000 artist grants from a total pool of $13,000. Two artists will each receive $4,500 and four artists will each receive $1,000. This is an international open call, and all visual media is eligible. The Hopper Prize provides a direct path to get your work in front of an international community of curators, artists, gallerists, and arts administrators. Additional exposure is available via a 30 artist shortlist, an online journal, and an Instagram account currently reaching over 175,000.Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PST on November 17, 2026.
GLEAM | 2027 Call for Light-Based ArtworkFeaturedOlbrich Botanical Gardens invites proposals for temporary, large-scale, light-based artwork for GLEAM, a public art exhibition situated within a 16-acre Midwest landscape and 10,000 square-foot tropical conservatory. The 2027 GLEAM exhibit will focus on works presenting a captivating environment, creating delight and connection through playful interactions, and energizing the gardens’ landscape with illuminated motion! Special consideration will be given to proposals that incorporate a kinetic element.Deadline: 11:59 p.m. CST on January 6, 2027.
Open Calls
2027 ArtFields Festival(Southeastern U.S.)Submit to the 2027 ArtFields Festival and be part of a unique celebration of art and community in Lake City, South Carolina. Selected artworks will be in one of the Southeast’s largest and most prestigious art events from April 9 to May 1, 2027, and in the running for more than $100,000 in cash prizes. There is a $25 application fee.Deadline: November 1, 2026.
International Art Frontier(International)This international prize includes prizes of exhibitions at two Moho Gallery venues in Cannaregio, Venice, including a final collective show of 12 finalists, plus four solo exhibitions for the winning artists from January to March 2027. The four winners also receive a €1,000 prize. There is a €35 entry fee for the first artwork and €20 each for additional artwork submissions.Deadline: November 4, 2026.
Arch Enemy Arts Call for Artists(International)Arch Enemy Arts is seeking submissions for an annual group exhibition in January 2027. This spotlight exhibition of new and emerging talent has no themes or direction in subject matter, although the gallery focuses on representational, dark surrealism, magical realism, post-graffiti, pop-surrealism, narrative, illustrative, and figurative work across a range of artistic mediums. The exhibition is open to artists worldwide, who are invited to submit up to three works for consideration.Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EST on November 13, 2026.
The John Ruskin Prize(International)This prize is open to entries from artists, designers, and makers in any stage of their career, working in any medium, from anywhere in the world. This year’s theme is Not for Present Delight, asking what it means to create with an awareness of consequence while also posing the challenge: must art serve a purpose beyond itself? Five winners will receive prizes totaling £10,000, and work will be selected for inclusion in an exhibition at Trinity Buoy Wharf, London.Deadline: 5 p.m. GMT on November 17, 2026.
2027 Beam Camp Project Open Call(International)Beam Center, located in Strafford, New Hampshire, seeks design proposals for an ambitious public artwork that will be brought to life through collaborations between youth, Beam Camp staff, and the selected proposer. Projects will be realized by a community of more than 100 young people at Beam Camp in July 2026. Selected project proposers receive a $5,000 award, and chosen projects will receive an approximately $15,000 fabrication budget.Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EST on November 30, 2026.
Wildlife Photographer of the Year(International)Alongside its conservation message, this prestigious global competition is hosted by London’s Natural History Museum to champion the work of photographers, whether professional or amateur, young or older, or using top-of-the-range equipment or smartphones. Photographers are eligible for myriad awards, with a Grand Title prize of £15,000. The entry fee is £35 (free for Young WPY contest).Deadline: 11:30 p.m. GMT on December 3, 2026.
Responsa Foundation Open Call for Textile Art(International)The Responsa Foundation champions projects that create meaningful social impact and foster public engagement. The organization is seeking textile artists to submit work for This Memory, a group exhibition taking place from September 22 to October 3, 2027, at Burgh House in Hampstead. Deadline: December 4, 2026.
Open Call for Public Art Proposals in Moab(Utah, National)Moab Arts is accepting proposals for 2027 public art projects. Proposals are welcome for sculpture, murals, three crosswalks, and sticker designs but may include other ideas for different media or locations around the city. Preference is given to local and regional artists.Deadline: 11:59 p.m. MST on December 6, 2026.
Material Works Art Award 2026(International)Material Works supports artists through one-time $2,500 awards in exchange for original pieces added to its growing contemporary art collection. The award recognizes artistic excellence and aims to promote career advancement through increasing visibility and exposure. There is a €40 application fee.Deadline: December 6, 2026, or when the first 300 artworks submitted, whichever comes first.
Grants
Artist Trust Fellowship Awards(Washington State)Artist Trust Fellowship Awards are merit-based awards of $10,000 to practicing professional artists of exceptional talent and ability residing in Washington State. These unrestricted awards are given annually to artists of any discipline in recognition of artistic excellence and dedication to their practice.Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PST on November 2, 2026.
MAKE Animation Thesis Grants(International)MAKE is proud to continue its annual grant program supporting senior animation students around the globe, championing and spotlighting emerging talent by directly funding original animated thesis projects (short films). First place is $2,000; second place is $1,000, and third place is $500.Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EST on November 6, 2026.
Asian Cultural Counsel Grants(Asia)ACC supports artists, scholars, arts professionals, and organizations through fellowships and grants that advance cultural exchange between the U.S. and Asia and within Asia. For individuals, the organization offers the six-month New York Fellowship, the one- to six-month Individual Fellowship, and the Graduate Fellowship for a student from Asia to study in the U.S.Deadline: 9:59 a.m. EST on November 10, 2026.
The Virigina A. Groot Foundation Grants(International)Each year, the Virginia A. Groot Foundation offers three grants to artists who have exceptional talent and a demonstrated ability in ceramic sculpture or sculpture of diverse mediums. The grants are organized into tiers, with the top award providing $60,000, the second award offering $30,000, and the third awarding $20,000.Deadline: January 9, 2027.
National Lottery Project Grants(U.K.)Individuals and organizations can apply to National Lottery Project Grants. These awards are designed to focus on specific projects with starting and ending dates including festivals and carnivals, dance, libraries, literature, museums, music, theater, or visual arts programs. There is no maximum threshold for the fund.Deadline: Rolling.
Black Artists Grant(U.K.)The Black Artists Grant offered by Creative Debuts is no-strings-attached financial support to help Black artists. Selected applicants receive £500, and applications are reviewed monthly.Deadline: Rolling.
The Adolf and Esther Gottlieb Emergency Grant (International)This program provides one-time financial assistance to qualified painters, printmakers, and sculptors whose needs resulted from an unforeseen catastrophic incident and who lack the resources to meet that situation. Awardees typically receive $5,000 and up to $15,000.Deadline: Rolling.
Pollock-Krasner Foundation Grant (International)The foundation welcomes applications from painters, sculptors, and artists working on paper, including printmakers. Grants are intended for one year and range up to $50,000. The artist’s circumstances determine the size of the grant, and professional exhibition history will be considered.Deadline: Rolling.
Residencies, Fellowships, & More
Sanford Underground Research Facility Artist-in-Residence (International)The SURF AiR program provides opportunities for artists to create work inspired by the Sanford Underground Research Facility, set in the Black Hills of South Dakota. At 4,850 feet deep, SURF is the deepest underground laboratory in the U.S. and is located in the former Homestake Gold Mine. The facility houses experiments in physics, biology, geology, and engineering. SURF AiR includes a four-week on-site visit in the summer and a one-week art installation/guest lecture visit in the fall. The selected artist will receive a stipend of $5,000 and may apply for up to $5,000 in additional funds to be used for the creation of artwork.Deadline: November 1, 2026.
Glen Arbor Arts Center Residency (International)The Glen Arbor Arts Center offers several opportunities for artist residencies each year. The program’s purpose is to provide visiting artists with a respite from daily responsibilities to enable them to concentrate on their work. Housing and studio space are provided for each two-week residency, and artists may work in disciplines of creative writing, visual art, photography, sculpture, fiber arts, ceramics, and music. There is a $35 application fee.Deadline: 2 p.m. EDT on November 5, 2026.
McKnight Printmaking Fellowship at Highpoint(Minnesota)The McKnight Artist & Culture Bearer Fellowships Program provides annual, unrestricted cash awards to outstanding mid-career Minnesota artists in 15 different creative disciplines. The fellowship includes an unrestricted $25,000 award, one year’s access to Highpoint’s state-of-the-art print shop, technical support from the fellowship coordinator, and more.Deadline: November 15, 2026.
Chulitna Lodge Wilderness Retreat (International)Chulitna Lodge Wilderness Retreat in Port Alsworth, Alaska, provides time, space, clarity, and facilities for creative professionals and researchers. Three ways to participate as an artist at Chulitna include a fellowship category with all expenses covered, a resident artist category with a reduced fee for room and board, and an honorary resident category for which the artist contributes fees and doesn’t not need a fill out an application.Deadline: 11:59 p.m. AST, November 28, 2026.
Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowships and Mentorships(International)Vital Impacts is dedicated to supporting photographers who capture compelling, solutions-focused environmental stories, and the organization is offering one $20,000 fellowship and six $5,000 fellowships. Recipients will have twelve months to develop their projects with support from Vital Impacts to publish and showcase their work. Additionally, ten emerging photographers will be chosen to participate in an intensive mentorship program.Deadline: November 30, 2026.
Jan Van Eyck Academie 2028 Residencies(International)The Jan van Eyck Academie welcomes around 36 participants annually from all over the world. Its 11-month residency opportunity is open to artists, designers, architects, curators, writers, and other artistic researchers and makers. Participants receive housing, studio space, a €1,500 stipend per month, plus additional benefits for duos, collectives, and artists with children.Deadline: November 30, 2026.
Bernheim Forest 2027 Artist-in-Residence Program(International)Located in Clermont, Kentucky, Bernheim Forest and Arboretum hosts an annual Artist-in-Residence Program that awards up to four residencies per year to artists whose work brings people closer to nature. The program includes a $2,500 stipend along with the opportunity to live at Bernheim Forest for six to eight weeks and create site specific work inspired by the immersive experience in the natural environment.Deadline: November 30, 2026.
Cove Park Awarded Residencies for 2027-28(International)Located in beautiful Argyll & Bute, Scotland, Cove Park awards funded residencies, in addition to travel, visa, materials, and access allowances when required. (Self-funded Open Residencies and subsidized winter residencies are open on a rolling basis.)Deadline: December 11, 2026.
Joshua Tree Highlands Artist Residency 2027-28(International)Joshua Tree Highlands Artist Residency offers time and space amidst the natural beauty of Joshua Tree National Park. Seven-week residencies include scholarship funds, housing, and studio space designed to accommodate a broad range of artistic activity and open studio events. There is a $45 application fee.Deadline: December 15, 2026.
Weaving Wonder Retreat at The Makerie(International)Jessie Mordine Young will be offering a three-day weaving retreat from June 4 to 6, 2027, at Black Cat Farm in Boulder, Colorado, care of The Makerie. Sixteen spots are open for participants with a price of $2,345, which includes three full workshop days, some meals, and other benefits. A scholarship is available for BIPOC artists that covers the entire workshop cost.Deadline: Until filled.
Bryson County Retreat(U.S.)This northern Florida retreat immerses visiting artists in the state’s beautiful nature on 200 private acres with easy access to the Santa Fe Swamp Wildlife Management Area and Lake Santa Fe. Bryson County Retreat is accepting applications from artists working in any medium for its 2027 residencies. Participation is free, and residents stay in one of three well-equipped houses with access to studio space and outdoor work space.Deadline: Rolling.
Smithereen Farm Winter Residency(International)Smithereen Farm offers affordable, shared, winter housing to farmers and agrarian-adjacent people and creatives. In the winter, its studio spaces and rooms in shared houses are generally rented for $350 per month, which includes access to common rooms, space for studio work or desks, utilities, fast Wi-Fi at Reversing Hall, a carpenter shop, sewing machines, video projection space, and access to the farm’s agricultural library.Deadline: Rolling.
Jackrabbit Studios Residency(International)Jackrabbit Studios is a creative sanctuary and retreat space in the Southern California High Desert that welcomes creatives, healing arts practitioners, and facilitators at any stage of practice to our five acres of secluded and sublime desert expanse to craft a residency tailored to your season of practice. Fees range from $450 per week to $2,000 per week, and pets are welcome for an additional fee.Deadline: Rolling.
